relationships.evidence_quote: Ablation of mTOR nearly eliminated NPY induction (Figure 6, E and G), indicating that mTOR was required for nerve injury–induced NPY elevation.

relationships.evidence_quote: mTOR ablation significantly blocked the nerve injury–increased STAT3 phosphorylation and its localization in the nucleus, along with reduced NPY induction

relationships.subject: neuropeptide Y
relationships.evidence_quote: Moreover, blocking Y2R also prevented NPY replenishment–induced AP increase in DRG neurons, suggesting that NPY elevates neuronal excitation primarily through Y2R in DRG

relationships.subject: mTOR
relationships.evidence_quote: selective ablation of mTOR in DRG neurons, rather than microglia, alleviated acute neuropathic pain in mice

key_findings: After SNI, mTOR is activated mainly in large DRG neurons and spinal microglia; neuronal but not microglial mTOR deletion alleviated pain.
mTOR drives NPY induction via STAT3 phosphorylation, and NPY acts on Y2R to enhance nociceptor excitability.
